claim_type_rationale: Wikipedia's 'List of national capitals' master article anchors the candidate universe of sovereign-state capitals (UN member + observer states, bold rows in the master) but does NOT carry a River column and does NOT define the target subset 'capitals that sit on a single primary perennial river'. The inclusion predicate is rebuilt entirely from per-capital prose per a two-part admission rule: (a) source-rule qualifier (per audit-cycle-7 BLOCKING) — each in-scope capital must have its own standalone English Wikipedia article; capitals whose EN URLs redirect to another capital's article (e.g., Comayagüela → Tegucigalpa) are OUT of scope before the river gate is applied; (b) strict gate (per audit-cycle-1 amendment #2) — each in-scope capital's own standalone EN article must foreground a single primary perennial river in the lede or infobox. Per audit-cycle-1 design review (re-confirmed verbatim in audit-cycle-2): this is closer to the philosophical-schools `candidate_rebuild` pattern than to a `partially_supplemented` pattern, because the load-bearing 'sits on a river' filter cannot be derived from any single master source. This is the 5th `candidate_rebuild` claim type instance in pkdb_bench, joining `major_philosophical_schools_founders_origins`, `major_religious_traditions_foundational_texts`, `major_western_philosophers_primary_works`, and `major_architectural_styles_landmark_buildings`.

collection_summary.approach: Pre-curation design pass (cycle-0 source exploration + audit-cycle-1 design review APPROVE-WITH-AMENDMENTS + audit-cycle-2 amendment re-confirmation) initially screened 60 sovereign-state capitals across 6 cycle-0 batches. Audit-cycle-1 post-staging review surfaced 2 BLOCKING strict-gate violations (Bratislava, Minsk) and a universe-completeness BLOCKING; cycle-2 repair dropped the 2 violations + added Brussels (cycle-1 miss) + Manila + 12 additional borderline candidates verified. Audit-cycle-2 BLOCKING said sweep was still incomplete; cycle-3 chose Path A and added 6 more batches (50 verifications, +10 INCLUDE / 40 EXCLUDE). Audit-cycle-3 BLOCKING #1 said common-knowledge bucketing wasn't sufficient evidence under a prose-sensitive gate (Riyadh precedent); audit-cycle-3 BLOCKING #2 said Riyadh/Wadi Hanifa doesn't fit the river-only title (wadi-not-perennial-river). Cycle-4 repair: completed remaining per-capital verification, dropped Riyadh, surfaced 7 new INCLUDEs (Havana/Almendares, Kingston/Hope, Roseau/Roseau River, Santo Domingo/Ozama, Bissau/Geba River, Georgetown/Demerara, Ulaanbaatar/Tuul). Audit-cycle-4 BLOCKING #1 estuary-policy-inconsistency → cycle-5 dropped Bissau + Georgetown. Audit-cycle-6 BLOCKING (scope) Capital-keyed framing → cycle-7 added Comayagüela. Audit-cycle-7 BLOCKING (factual) Comayagüela has no standalone English Wikipedia article (the EN URL redirects to Tegucigalpa) → cycle-8 dropped Comayagüela: under the declared source rule (every included capital admitted by its own per-capital English article), Comayagüela is out of scope; Capital-keyed framing still applies, with the source-rule qualifier that each capital must have a standalone EN article. Final staged universe: 56 capitals PASS the strict gate AND have standalone EN articles. Per-row data partitioned by source role: Wikipedia 'List of national capitals' master defines Capital + Country + Continent (3 of 4 cells); per-capital Wikipedia article defines River + admission decision (1 of 4 cells). EXACT FINAL ACCOUNTING: 56 staged INCLUDE + 145 per-capital-verified EXCLUDE + 2 cycle-2 strict-gate-violation drops = 203 per-capital admission verdicts covering every UN-member sovereign-state capital with a standalone EN article + every co-official joint-capital with a standalone EN article + Taiwan/Kosovo contested-sovereign cases.
collection_summary.continent_skew_note: Europe accounts for 23 of 56 staged rows (41%). The sweep arc steadily diluted the Europe-weighting: cycle-0/cycle-1 was 22/42 (52%); cycle-3 added 9 non-European INCLUDEs vs 1 European (Vaduz); cycle-4 added 5 net non-European INCLUDEs (Ulaanbaatar; Havana/Kingston/Roseau/Santo Domingo) vs 0 European, also dropped Riyadh; cycle-5 dropped 2 non-European (Bissau Africa + Georgetown SA) for estuary-policy consistency; cycle-7 added Comayagüela (NA) which cycle-8 reverted (no standalone EN article — fails source rule). Across cycles 0–8 the non-European staged share went from 19/42 → 33/56 (59%). The remaining Europe-leaning is structural rather than cycle-bias: European capitals historically founded along major rivers (Danube, Vistula, Thames, Seine, Tiber, Tagus) by medieval city-development patterns, while non-European capitals are more often coastal (post-colonial era), planned-inland-without-river (Brasília, Abuja, Canberra, Naypyidaw), or desert/highland-without-river (Tehran, Ankara, Addis Ababa). Oceania has zero rows: every Oceanic sovereign-state capital was individually verified (Canberra, Wellington, Apia, Funafuti, Honiara, Ngerulmud, Nukuʻalofa, Palikir, Port Moresby, Port Vila, South Tarawa, Suva, Yaren, Dili) and none foregrounds a single primary river in its per-capital article lede or infobox.
collection_summary.river_grounding: 56 of 56 rows — each row's River is the single foregrounded primary perennial river per its own standalone English Wikipedia article's lede or infobox. Admission-gating rule applied strictly per audit-cycle-1 amendment #2: capitals where the per-capital article does NOT foreground a single primary perennial river (multi-river / confluence / no-river / estuary / wadi) are excluded even if a river is mentioned in body text. Source-rule qualifier per audit-cycle-7 BLOCKING: each included capital must have its own standalone English Wikipedia article — co-official capitals without standalone articles (e.g., Comayagüela, whose EN URL redirects to Tegucigalpa) are OUT of scope.
collection_summary.river_format: Bare river name (no 'River' suffix) where the river name is unambiguous (Thames, Seine, Danube, Nile, Tiber, Congo, Niger, Mekong, etc.). 'River' suffix retained for 3 rows in the live CSV to disambiguate the cell from the city PK or country name: 'Kabul River' for Kabul (Afghanistan — same-name city), 'Roseau River' for Roseau (Dominica — same-name city), and 'Suriname River' for Paramaribo (Suriname — same as country name).
collection_summary.country_format: Per the master article's Country/Territory column — UN-recognized sovereign-state names. 'Congo' for Republic of the Congo (Brazzaville) and 'Democratic Republic of the Congo' for DRC (Kinshasa) per master convention (audit-cycle-1 amendment #4: use master for Country; do not deviate from master form even where ambiguous).
collection_summary.continent_format: Closed 6-value vocabulary per master's Continent column: Africa / Asia / Europe / North America / South America / Oceania. Edge-case continent assignments (per master): Tbilisi → Asia (master says Asia/Europe; staged as Asia per Asian-side-of-Caucasus convention); Astana → Asia; Cairo → Africa; Moscow → Europe.

master_article.role: universe-anchor + Capital + Country + Continent (3 of 4 cells per audit-cycle-1 amendment #4 — source-role separation). Filters applied at the universe-anchor stage: (a) sovereign-state filter per audit-cycle-1 amendment #5 — only bold UN-member + observer-state rows are in scope; territories, dependencies (Hamilton Bermuda, Pago Pago American Samoa, etc.), and disputed entities excluded; (b) standalone-EN-article source-rule per audit-cycle-7 BLOCKING — each in-scope capital must have its own standalone English Wikipedia article (capitals whose EN URLs redirect to another capital's article, e.g., Comayagüela → Tegucigalpa, are OUT of scope upstream of the river gate). After both upstream filters, the per-capital article supplies the River + admission decision.
